rhetorical_skeleton.writing_objective: Sell the critical need for Multi-AP Coordination (MAP-Co) in next-gen WLANs (Wi-Fi 7 / 802.11be and WiGig / 802.11ay) by highlighting the limitations of single-AP systems in dense environments.
key_components: Evolution of WLAN standards (802.11n -> ac -> ax -> be/ay)
The gap: Single-AP surveys exist, but MAP-Co surveys are missing
Explicit statement of contributions (Taxonomy, Lesson Learned, Future Directions)

rhetorical_skeleton.writing_objective: Establish the foundational architectures (Centralized vs Distributed) before diving into protocol specifics, creating a clear structural mental model for the reader.
Detail the prerequisite phase for coordination: acquiring Channel State Information (CSI) in a multi-node environment.
key_components: Detailed MAC frame exchange descriptions (NDPA, NDP, Beamforming Report)

rhetorical_skeleton.writing_objective: Analyze the core technical mechanisms for coordinated interference management and resource allocation.
Propose forward-looking research paths including AI/ML integration and specific challenges for mmWave/THz bands.

visual_roadmap.layout_logic: The paper strictly follows a 'Process Flow' logic: Architecture -> Channel Acquisition -> Scheduling/Transmission. Critically, it employs a recurring 'Summary and Lesson Learned' block at the end of every major technical section to synthesize findings immediately.
required_table_types: Gap Analysis Table (Current WLAN vs Emerging WLAN studies)
Taxonomy Table (Pros/Cons of Explicit vs Implicit Sounding in MC/MA architectures)

writing_style_secrets.phrasing_patterns: Consistently uses the phrase 'Summary and Lesson Learned' as a subsection title. Uses 'In this vein,' to transition to related works. High density of technical acronyms defined early in a dedicated table.
writing_style_secrets.technical_depth_management: Separates the high-level 'Architecture' (Section III) from the protocol-level 'Channel Sounding' (Section IV). This prevents the reader from getting lost in MAC frame details before understanding the system topology.

top_3_tips: Implement a 'Lessons Learned' subsection at the end of every major technical block. This provides 'checkpoints' for the reader to consolidate complex info.
Create a rigorous taxonomy table that cross-references methods (e.g., Sounding Types) against architectures (MC vs MA) with pros/cons.
Strictly separate the 'Network Design' (Topology) from 'Data Transmission' (Protocol Operations) to manage complexity.
mistakes_to_avoid: Avoid discussing protocol frame exchanges (NDP, NDPA) before defining the network nodes (Master Controller, Slave AP) and their hierarchy.
Do not mix 802.11be (Sub-6GHz) and 802.11ay (mmWave) details indiscriminately; clarify which standard supports which feature.
Don't ignore the 'overhead' implications. This paper explicitly analyzes communication/computation overhead for every method.
